source:
Jamie: Cut the podcast episodes to twenty minutes. Our commuters bail out before the guest's third story.
Casey: Keep the forty-minute format. The whole reason listeners write in is that we let guests build an argument instead of doing headline snippets.
Jamie: We can keep depth and still edit harder. The analytics chart drops sharply after minute twenty-three.
Casey: That chart counts people who finish later in the week as partial listens. You are treating an app quirk as an editorial mandate.
Jamie: Sponsors buy completed listens, not good intentions.
Casey: Sponsors also renew because the show sounds different from every chopped-up interview feed.

extraction.mainQuestion: Should the podcast cut episodes to twenty minutes or keep the forty-minute format?

positions.label: Cut to twenty minutes
positions.thesis: The podcast should cut episodes to twenty minutes because listeners and sponsors reward completed listens.
positions.steelman: If most listeners drop after the early segment, tighter editing could improve completion and sponsor value.

groundingQuotes.quote: Cut the podcast episodes to twenty minutes.

positions.label: Keep forty minutes
positions.thesis: The podcast should keep the forty-minute format because depth is the show's differentiator.
positions.steelman: Longer interviews may preserve the reason listeners and sponsors value the show even if completion metrics look weaker.

claims.statement: The analytics show a sharp listener drop after minute twenty-three.

resolution.condition: Audit the analytics treatment of partial and delayed listens.

groundingQuotes.quote: The analytics chart drops sharply after minute twenty-three.

claims.statement: The drop-off chart is distorted by how the app counts later finishes.

resolution.condition: Check whether delayed completions are classified as partial listens.

groundingQuotes.quote: That chart counts people who finish later in the week as partial listens.

disagreementCandidates.question: Does the completion metric show a real listener problem or an app-counting artifact?
disagreementCandidates.summary: Jamie treats the drop-off chart as decisive; Casey says the metric is distorted.

participantStances.stance: The chart shows episodes are too long.

disagreementCandidates.resolutionCondition: Review completion definitions and delayed-listen data.

caveats: The source asserts analytics behavior but does not provide the chart itself.
